Rule_Name: Candidate rack capacity must come from the selected rack record
Rule_Description: A candidate rack's total Rack_Units must be read from the actual candidate Rack catalogue record; no universal rack size is assumed.
Condition: Rack_Units is present for the candidate rack.
Source_Title: ASHRAE Handbook — Data Centers and Telecommunication Facilities; Open Rack V3 Base Specification
Page_Section_Table_Equation: 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; 2.3 Datacom Equipment; 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom Rooms / facility infrastructure; Chapter 20, Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom equipment racks; datacom rooms / facility infrastructure; Reused through Parts 1–4 rule traceability; Open Rack V3 Base Specification
Evidence: Rack U is an explicit rack product attribute; ASHRAE describes U/RU as the vertical rack dimension.
Limitations: No universal 42U/45U/48U value is introduced.
Notes: Use only the selected rack record.

Rule_Name: Equipment mounting height must be explicit before U capacity can be evaluated
Rule_Description: Each rack-mounted equipment item contributing to Rack occupancy must have a source-supported mounting height in U. If required equipment U is missing, the U-demand calculation is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
Condition: Any required equipment lacks a source-supported U value.
Source_Title: ASHRAE Handbook — Data Centers and Telecommunication Facilities; Open Rack V3 Base Specification
Page_Section_Table_Equation: 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; 2.3 Datacom Equipment; 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom Rooms / facility infrastructure; Chapter 20, Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom equipment racks; datacom rooms / facility infrastructure; Reused through Parts 1–4 rule traceability; Open Rack V3 Base Specification
Evidence: Rack equipment is mounted using rack-unit dimensions; the rule only requires explicit equipment-side input.
Limitations: No equipment U values are invented or estimated by Rack.
Notes: Underlying equipment sizing remains owned by its source domain.

Rule_Name: Occupied U is the sum of the U demand of equipment assigned to the rack
Rule_Description: For a defined rack assignment, occupied U is the sum of each equipment item's U demand multiplied by its quantity. The result is deployment occupancy, not a product catalogue field.
Condition: All assigned equipment U values are available.
Source_Title: ASHRAE Handbook — Data Centers and Telecommunication Facilities
Page_Section_Table_Equation: 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; 2.3 Datacom Equipment; 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom Rooms / facility infrastructure; Chapter 20, Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom equipment racks; datacom rooms / facility infrastructure; Reused through Parts 1–4 rule traceability
Evidence: The arithmetic aggregates the vertical mounting requirement of rack-mounted equipment.
Limitations: Requires explicit rack assignment and equipment U values.
Notes: Do not include non-rack-mounted equipment.

Rule_Name: Remaining rack U is usable rack U minus occupied U
Rule_Description: Remaining U is calculated only after the rack's usable U and assigned equipment occupancy are known.
Condition: Usable_Rack_U and Occupied_U are both available and refer to the same rack scope.
Source_Title: ASHRAE Handbook — Data Centers and Telecommunication Facilities
Page_Section_Table_Equation: 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; 2.3 Datacom Equipment; 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom Rooms / facility infrastructure; Chapter 20, Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom equipment racks; datacom rooms / facility infrastructure; Reused through Parts 1–4 rule traceability
Evidence: Provides a direct residual-capacity calculation; no utilization threshold is introduced.
Limitations: Part 0 does not provide deployed occupied U; this is a later deployment input.
Notes: Use product-specific usable U if documented; otherwise use the appropriate rack capacity representation.

Rule_Name: U-based rack count is a theoretical lower bound, not final feasible rack count
Rule_Description: When total equipment U demand and candidate rack usable U are known, the minimum U-only lower bound is the ceiling of total U demand divided by usable U per rack.
Condition: Both inputs are positive and refer to the same deployment scope.
Source_Title: ASHRAE Handbook — Data Centers and Telecommunication Facilities
Page_Section_Table_Equation: 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; 2.3 Datacom Equipment; 2.2 Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom Rooms / facility infrastructure; Chapter 20, Datacom Equipment Racks; Datacom equipment racks; datacom rooms / facility infrastructure; Reused through Parts 1–4 rule traceability
Evidence: Ceiling arithmetic gives the smallest integer rack count satisfying U capacity alone.
Limitations: Depth, width, mounting, weight, structural and placement constraints may increase actual feasible rack count.
Notes: Never report this lower bound as final feasibility.

Rule_Name: Actual feasible rack count must satisfy constraints beyond U
Rule_Description: A U-based lower bound cannot be promoted to an actual feasible rack count until depth, width/mounting, weight/structural and placement constraints are also evidenced.
Inputs: U_Lower_Bound; Depth_Check; Width_Mounting_Check; Weight_Check; Structural_Check; Placement_Check
Input_Source: Rack + Server + Networking + Storage + Compatibility + facility inputs
Condition: Any material physical constraint is unresolved or violated.
Source_Title: ASHRAE Handbook — Data Centers and Telecommunication Facilities; Data center power minimization with placement optimization of liquid-cooled servers and free air cooling; AI Data Center Energy Performance Framework — Integrated Design Principles

Evidence: Rack planning involves physical dimensions and placement constraints; research shows placement is not reducible to a single capacity dimension.
Limitations: Final Rack feasibility integration belongs to Part 5.
Notes: Research support is principle-level, not a universal threshold.

Rule_Name: Equipment depth must not exceed the applicable rack usable internal depth
Rule_Description: For a candidate rack, compare each equipment's required depth to the rack's applicable usable internal depth. If the rack-side depth value is estimated, the comparison remains evidence-limited.
Condition: Both depth values are available and their measurement scopes are compatible.
Source_Title: APC NetShelter SX AR3350; Vertiv VR3350 Product and Submittal Drawing
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Product specifications; Reused through Parts 1–4 rule traceability; Physical Characteristics; Load Rating; Drawing
Evidence: Manufacturer documentation distinguishes rack external dimensions from usable equipment depth; physical fit therefore requires the applicable internal/mounting dimension.
Limitations: Part 0 marks Usable_Internal_Depth_mm as ESTIMATED for all 12 records.
Notes: Do not treat estimated depth as verified.

Rule_Name: Estimated rack usable depth must remain evidence-limited
Rule_Description: If Usable_Internal_Depth_mm is used and its Part 0 status is ESTIMATED, the resulting depth decision must preserve ESTIMATED/LIMITED evidence status rather than being upgraded to verified.
Condition: Status is ESTIMATED.
Source_Title: Vertiv VR3350 Product and Submittal Drawing
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Physical Characteristics; Load Rating; Drawing
Evidence: Part 0 explicitly identifies usable internal depth as estimated; manufacturer drawings should be preferred for final product-specific verification.
Limitations: No automatic correction or silent promotion of estimated values.
Notes: Evidence limitation only; not automatic failure.

Rule_Name: External rack width must be distinguished from equipment mounting width/standard
Rule_Description: Rack external width must not be used as a substitute for the equipment mounting interface. The applicable mounting standard/interface must be checked separately.
Condition: Candidate rack and equipment mounting interface are both identified.
Source_Title: ASHRAE Handbook — Data Centers and Telecommunication Facilities; Open Rack V3 Base Specification; Rittal Open Rack V3 (ORV3)
Organisation: ASHRAE; Open Compute Project; Rittal / OCP

Evidence: ASHRAE distinguishes rack/cabinet physical dimensions from equipment mounting standards; OCP documents distinct 21-inch/19-inch interfaces.
Limitations: No universal 19-inch assumption; ORV3-specific interfaces remain product/context dependent.
Notes: Compatibility domain owns detailed equipment matching.

Rule_Name: Rack mounting interface must be explicitly supported for the equipment class
Rule_Description: A rack candidate is physically mountable only when its documented mounting interface/standard and required rails or brackets are compatible with the equipment's physical mounting requirements. Detailed compatibility remains Compatibility-owned.
Condition: Required mounting interface evidence is present and consistent.
Source_Title: Open Rack V3 Base Specification; Vertiv VR3350 Product and Submittal Drawing
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Open Rack V3 Base Specification; Physical Characteristics; Load Rating; Drawing
Evidence: Manufacturer/OCP documentation demonstrates that mounting interfaces and accessories are product-specific.
Limitations: Do not duplicate compatibility matrix logic.
Notes: Rack evaluates the rack-side physical constraint only.

Rule_Name: Rail-kit requirements must be preserved as physical deployment dependencies
Rule_Description: If the selected rack requires a rail kit or mounting accessory, that requirement must be carried into deployment configuration rather than assumed to be included.
Condition: Rail_Kit_Required is Yes or another explicit requirement is documented.
Source_Title: Vertiv VR3350 Product and Submittal Drawing
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Physical Characteristics; Load Rating; Drawing
Evidence: Vertiv product documentation identifies rack hardware/accessories and mounting arrangements as product-specific.
Limitations: Exact equipment-to-rail model mapping remains outside Rack ownership.
Notes: Carry the dependency; do not invent rail models.

Rule_Name: Total equipment weight is the sum of weights of equipment assigned to the rack
Rule_Description: For a defined rack assignment, total equipment weight is the sum of equipment weight multiplied by quantity. Rack empty weight is not part of equipment load unless the applicable load rating explicitly requires another basis.
Condition: All equipment weights required for the assignment are source-supported.
Source_Title: APC NetShelter SX AR3350; Vertiv VR3350 Product and Submittal Drawing
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Product specifications; Reused through Parts 1–4 rule traceability; Physical Characteristics; Load Rating; Drawing
Evidence: Rack manufacturers publish load ratings separately from rack self-weight; the rule preserves that distinction.
Limitations: Requires equipment-side weights; no Rack-side estimates are invented.
Notes: Use the applicable load basis for the deployment scenario.

Rule_Name: Equipment load must not exceed the applicable rack load rating
Rule_Description: Compare total equipment load with the rack's applicable documented load capacity. Static and dynamic/rolling ratings are separate; do not substitute one for the other.
Condition: Applicable load mode and both values are known.
Source_Title: APC NetShelter SX AR3350; Vertiv VR3350 Product and Submittal Drawing; ZetaFrame Cabinet System
Organisation: Schneider Electric / APC; Vertiv; Chatsworth Products
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Product specifications; Reused through Parts 1–4 rule traceability; Physical Characteristics; Load Rating; Drawing; Product specifications
Evidence: Manufacturer sources publish distinct static and dynamic ratings, demonstrating that the load basis matters.
Limitations: Dynamic_Load_Capacity_kg is estimated for 8 Part 0 records; such cases remain evidence-limited.
Notes: No universal safety margin is introduced.

Rule_Name: Estimated dynamic load capacity cannot be treated as verified
Rule_Description: When a deployment decision uses Dynamic_Load_Capacity_kg and Part 0 marks it ESTIMATED, the result must be labelled evidence-limited.
Condition: Dynamic load status is ESTIMATED.
Source_Title: Vertiv VR3350 Product and Submittal Drawing
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Physical Characteristics; Load Rating; Drawing
Evidence: Part 0 identifies eight dynamic-load values as estimated and four as verified.
Limitations: Manufacturer/model-specific verification is required before final high-confidence use.
Notes: Evidence limitation only.

Rule_Name: Rack physical load capacity is not a substitute for facility structural evidence
Rule_Description: Rack-level static/dynamic load ratings do not by themselves establish floor, anchoring, seismic, point-load or other facility structural feasibility. Missing facility structural evidence must remain an evidence gap.
Inputs: Rack_Load_Rating; Floor_Loading; Point_Load; Anchoring; Seismic_Rating; Structural_Support
Condition: Facility structural requirements are not available or not linked to the rack deployment.
Source_Title: ZetaFrame Cabinet System; AI Data Center Energy Performance Framework — Integrated Design Principles

Evidence: High-density AI infrastructure increases the importance of structural support; rack product load rating and facility structural capacity are different evidence layers.
Limitations: Facility engineering is outside Rack catalogue ownership; no structural threshold is invented.
Notes: Part 5 may integrate this evidence later.

Rule_Name: Rack placement cannot be evaluated using U capacity alone when documented physical constraints apply
Rule_Description: A rack assignment must preserve all material documented physical constraints relevant to the equipment mix, including U, depth, mounting, weight and placement dependencies. Sufficient U alone is not proof of physical fit.
Condition: Any material physical constraint exists beyond U capacity.
Source_Title: Data center power minimization with placement optimization of liquid-cooled servers and free air cooling; Experimental and optimization research of the rack thermal environment based on dynamic server power

Limitations: Research context is thermal/placement focused; no universal spacing or utilization threshold is derived.
Notes: Cooling optimization itself remains out of scope.

Rule_Name: Greenfield and Brownfield rack capacity must be represented differently
Rule_Description: Greenfield evaluation may select a candidate rack based on documented product capacity; Brownfield evaluation must include existing rack identity, existing occupancy and remaining physical capacity before reuse is considered.
Condition: Scenario is explicitly GREENFIELD or BROWNFIELD.

Evidence: ASHRAE retrofit guidance highlights physical-density and structural constraints in existing facilities; Part 1 therefore requires existing-state evidence rather than assuming free capacity.
Limitations: No universal reuse percentage or free-space assumption is introduced.
Notes: Final feasibility remains Part 5.

Rule_Name: Brownfield available rack capacity requires explicit existing occupancy
Rule_Description: For an existing rack, available U can be derived only when the rack's usable capacity and existing occupied U are known. Unused-looking space is not automatically treated as available.
Condition: Both existing capacity and existing occupancy are known.
Source_Title: AI Data Center Energy Performance Framework — Retrofit & Modernization Strategies
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Retrofit & Modernization
Evidence: Retrofit planning requires assessment of existing conditions; the arithmetic expresses residual physical capacity without assuming all visible space is reusable.
Limitations: Does not address final compatibility, cooling, power or facility feasibility.
Notes: Use actual inventory evidence.

Rule_Name: Rack Cabinet, Rack System and Rack Frame must remain distinct in rule inputs
Rule_Description: The candidate entity level must be preserved because a rack frame/system may expose different mounting, enclosure or accessory interfaces than a conventional rack cabinet.
Condition: Entity level is available for the candidate record.
